findings.title: WorkflowNavigator sweep sites contradict the design's own TD-3 exclusion
findings.description: The site table (line 36), the component table (line 75), and work step 4 (line 90) direct sweeping 3 `WorkflowNavigator.ts` sites. But all three are `SliceStatus` sites, not `NormalizedStatus` sites: `WorkflowNavigator.ts:312` and `:345` compare `slice.status` where `slice` is `status.activeSlice` of type `SliceStatus`, and `:588` assigns `status: 'complete'` to a `SliceStatus` return value. TD-3 (lines 104–106) explicitly rules these out: "`SliceStatus.status`... Its `'complete'` member is incidental overlap in spelling, not the same type... Left untouched." Following the table would conflate the two unions TD-3 forbids conflating — and since `slice.status === STATUS.Complete` still compiles (both are strings), the compiler will not catch it, defeating the slice's own purpose for these sites. Conversely, honoring TD-3 leaves three literals that the success criterion (line 135, "zero matches in the six swept files", which includes `WorkflowNavigator.ts`) then flags as failures. The same root problem hits the functional requirement directly: the FR grep excludes only `types.ts:3-6` but not `types.ts:269` (`SliceStatus`'s `'complete'` member), so as literally specified the criterion is unsatisfiable while TD-3 stands. The row, step 4, TD-3, and the FR/grep need reconciliation before implementation — the WorkflowNavigator row should most likely read 0 sites.

findings.title: "Every production-code site" claim excludes a real CLI site without discussion
findings.description: The Overview promises "every production-code site that assigns or compares a `NormalizedStatus` value as a bare string literal", but the scope (line 29) restricts the sweep to `packages/core/src`. `packages/cli/src/commands/arch.ts:189` is a production bare-literal comparison (`init.slices.filter((s) => s.status === 'complete')`) against a value produced by `deriveEntryStatus` (a `NormalizedStatus`) or the `'unknown'` sentinel — the same class of site this slice exists to eliminate, in a file that already imports `STATUS` (arch.ts line 8), making the fix trivial. Either the Overview's "every production-code site" claim should be narrowed to core, or this site should be swept. As written, the stated goal is not met by the scoped work.

findings.title: Factual claim about test files is demonstrably false
findings.description: The document asserts "grep confirms zero `.test.ts` files assert against these literals directly (tests exercise behavior through parsers/fixtures, not string comparison)". This is false: numerous `.test.ts` files assert these literals directly — e.g. `packages/core/tests/introspection/statusNormalizer.test.ts:7` (`expect(normalizeStatus(input)).toBe('complete')`), `taskFileParser.test.ts:54`, `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts:47-48`, `WorkflowNavigator.test.ts:71`, `slicePlanParser.test.ts:15`, and CLI/MCP test files. The conclusion (no test changes needed) still holds — swept values are identical strings, so string assertions remain valid — but the stated evidence base is wrong and should be corrected to that reasoning, since the current claim misrepresents the regression guard's nature.

findings.title: Site-count arithmetic and walkthrough numbers do not reconcile
findings.description: Minor inventory inaccuracies that should be corrected when the scope contradiction above is fixed: the `types.ts` row says "5 (of 8 total)" sweepable, but the file has 4 `STATUS`-definition literals + 3 `inferredStatus` union literals (one line) + 1 `SliceStatus` literal = 8, of which only 3 sweep per the design's own rules. The verification walkthrough's "Before: ~75" (line 150) does not match a grep of `packages/core/src` (~66 occurrences by my count), and the "After" enumeration (4 + 3 + 4 = 11, line 151) sits awkwardly against the "zero matches" FR. None of these change the work, but a mechanical-sweep design lives and dies by an accurate count.

findings.title: Step 1's build-coupling rationale is incorrect (harmless)
findings.description: Step 1 claims retyping `TaskFileResult.inferredStatus` and sweeping `taskFileParser.ts` "must land together, or the intermediate state fails to build". Neither intermediate state fails: a bare `'complete'` literal is assignable to `NormalizedStatus` (a widening), and `STATUS.Complete` is assignable to the narrower three-member union. Landing them together is still good practice; the stated compile-failure justification is simply wrong and should not be relied on as an ordering constraint.
